subject: mathematics
question_text: If A is the matrix with rows (1, 2) and (3, 4), B is the matrix with rows (3, 8) and (4, 2), and 2X + A = B, then find X.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 5 MATRICES, Very Short Answer question 4, book p.31. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split gives one mark to rearranging 2X + A = B into 2X = B − A and one to the subtraction and the halving, because the rearrangement is the step a student can do without touching a single number. SECOND ROW OF B: the stem gives B's second row as (4, 2). The work order records that the book's own working subtracts 4 − 3 and 2 − 4, which confirms that row. NEAR-DUPLICATE, recorded rather than merged: ts_ipe_m1a_mat_vsaq_solve_for_x already in this unit is the same question from Baby Bullet-Q with B's second row printed as (7, 2), which gives the whole-number answer X = rows (1, 3) and (2, −1). The two books disagree on one row, so both cards are kept and the ids say which row each carries; this card's answer has the fraction 1/2 in it and that is correct for the row (4, 2). Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would get X out of the equation 2X + A = B.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Make X the subject
steps.margin_note: First mark. Matrices are added and subtracted entry by entry, so 2X + A = B rearranges exactly like an ordinary equation. A and B are both 2×2, so B − A is defined.
steps.memory_tip: Treat 2X + A = B like a number equation: move A across, then divide by 2.

recall.must_convey: That 2X + A = B is rearranged to 2X = B − A, and B − A is found entry by entry.
accept: take A to the other side so two X equals B minus A
subtract A from both sides then work out B minus A
rearrange to two X equals B minus A and subtract entry by entry
A ni other side ki teeskoni two X equals B minus A rasukovali
move A across and find the difference of the two matrices

steps.why: Matrix addition and subtraction follow the same cancellation rules as numbers, because they act on each position separately. Nothing here needs matrix multiplication.
common_mistakes: Computing A − B and getting every sign wrong.
Subtracting the entries from the wrong positions.

steps.label: Subtract, then halve every entry
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Dividing a matrix by 2 divides every entry by 2. One entry here is 1, so X carries the fraction 1/2 — that is the correct answer, not a rounding error.
steps.memory_tip: A scalar reaches every entry. Half of 1 is 1/2, so leave the fraction as it is.
lines: X = ½(B − A), so halve every entry.

recall.must_convey: That X is half of B − A, giving rows (1, 3) and (1/2, −1).
accept: divide every entry by two so X is one three and half minus one
half of B minus A gives rows one three and one by two minus one
halve each entry, one of them stays as a half
prathi entry ni two tho divide cheste X vasthundi
X equals one, three, one half and minus one

steps.why: Scalar multiplication reaches every entry, so dividing the matrix by 2 is one division per position. Substituting X back gives 2X + A = B, which is the check.
common_mistakes: Writing the entry 1/2 as 1 because it does not look like a whole number.
